summary: Ella Rebe Durand was the wife of Sir Mortimer Durand, British Minister at Tehran. In the autumn of 1899 they left the Legation with a party of servants, muleteers, and an escort and rode for eleven weeks, about twelve hundred miles, through Western Persia: south by Kum and Kashan to Ispahan, west through the Bakhtiari mountains to the Karun river, down to Ahwaz, Shuster, Dizful, and the ruins of Susa, then north through Luristan by Khurramabad, Burujird, and Sultanabad, and back to Tehran in mid-December. She describes how a travelling camp was organized, the roads and river crossings, the tribal chiefs who received them, the towns and villages, and life at the Legation and at Gulhek. It has twenty-two plates from photographs by Sévroguine of Tehran and by Ernest Rennie of the Diplomatic Service, six drawings in the text, and a map of the route.
